title: UnitBox: An Advanced Object Detection Network

problem.summary: Existing deep CNN object detectors regress the four bounding-box coordinates as four independent variables with an unnormalized l2 loss, which ignores that the bounds are correlated and skews the penalty toward large objects, hurting localization accuracy.
statements: Bounding box regression in deep CNN detectors treats the four box bounds as independent variables optimized separately under l2 loss, contrary to the observation that they are correlated.
The unnormalized l2 loss penalizes errors on large boxes more than small ones, so networks focus on larger objects and ignore smaller ones.
Traditional region proposal stages are both a localization bottleneck and a computational bottleneck for real-time deployment.

evidence.quote: However, existing deep CNN methods assume the object bounds to be four independent variables, which could be regressed by the `2 loss separately.
This assumption violates the fact that the bounds of an object are highly correlated.
This unbalance results in that the CNNs focus more on larger objects while ignore smaller ones.

background.summary: The paper builds on the three-step detection pipeline (region proposals, CNN classification, box regression) and on DenseBox's pixel-wise fully convolutional detection, arguing that both proposal-based methods and DenseBox's independent l2 box regression are flawed.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN (RPN)
relatedWork.relation: prior proposal mechanism whose fixed anchor scales/aspect ratios struggle with shape variation
relatedWork.quote: since the scales and aspect ratios of anchor boxes are pre-designed and fixed, the RPN shows difficult to handle the object candidates with large shape variations

relatedWork.name: DenseBox
relatedWork.relation: closest pixel-wise fully convolutional baseline; regresses four distances independently under l2 loss
relatedWork.quote: However, DenseBox optimizes the four-side distances as four independent variables, under the simplistic `2 loss

relatedWork.name: Selective Search / EdgeBoxes
relatedWork.relation: traditional proposal generators criticized for fragility and cost
relatedWork.quote: are sensitive to the local appearance changes, e.g., partial occlusion, where those algorithms are very likely to fail.

evidence.quote: In this pipeline, the region proposal algorithm constitutes a major bottleneck in terms of localization effectiveness, as well as efficiency.
DenseBox has to perform detection on image pyramids, which unavoidably affects the efficiency of the framework.

solution.summary: UnitBox is a fully convolutional pixel-wise detector built on VGG-16 that uses a new IoU loss, regressing the four box bounds jointly as a single unit so that training directly maximizes predicted/ground-truth overlap.
solution.approach: Regress all four bounds jointly with an IoU-based loss L = -ln(IoU) inside a two-branch fully convolutional network that predicts pixel-wise confidence and box heatmaps.
components: IoU loss layer (L = -ln(IoU)) with closed-form forward/backward passes
confidence branch on VGG stage-4 with sigmoid cross-entropy loss
bounding-box branch on VGG stage-5 with a single convolutional layer and ReLU for non-negativity
up-sample and crop layers aligning predictions to input image size
variable-scale (multi-scale) training enabled by scale-normalized IoU

evidence.quote: we firstly introduce a novel Intersection over Union (IoU ) loss function for bounding box prediction, which regresses the four bounds of a predicted box as a whole unit.
instead of optimizing four coordinates independently, the IoU loss considers the bounding box as a unit.
we remove the fully connected layers and add two branches of fully convolutional layers to predict the pixel-wise bounding boxes and classification scores

experiments.summary: The authors fine-tune UnitBox on WiderFace and evaluate face detection on the FDDB benchmark, ablating IoU loss against an otherwise identical l2-loss variant (UnitBox-l2) in terms of convergence, ROC, scale robustness, and speed.

evidence.quote: the proposed UnitBox has achieved the best detection result on FDDB among all published methods.
the model with IoU loss converges more quickly and steadily than the one with `2 loss.

limitations.summary: Evaluation is restricted to face detection on a single benchmark (FDDB), and the box-generation stage relies on face-specific heuristics such as fitting ellipses to the confidence map.
items: No generic object-detection results (e.g., PASCAL VOC or COCO) are reported; only the face detection task is evaluated.
Post-processing of heatmaps is face-specific (ellipse fitting on thresholded confidence maps) rather than a general detection decoding scheme.
The paper reports no numeric accuracy table; results are shown as ROC curves only.

evidence.quote: we apply the proposed IoU loss as well as the UnitBox on face detection task, and report our experimental results on the FDDB benchmark
firstly we fit the faces by ellipses on the thresholded confidence heatmaps.

futureDirections.direction: Extend IoU loss and UnitBox beyond face detection to other object localization and detection tasks.
futureDirections.quote: We believe that the IoU loss layer as well as the UnitBox will be of great value to other object localization and detection tasks.

applications.detail: UnitBox is applied to face detection and attains the best published FDDB performance; authors are affiliated with Megvii Inc.
applications.quote: We apply UnitBox on face detection task and achieve the best performance among all published methods on the FDDB benchmark.

applications.detail: The introduction names pedestrian detection among the application areas served by CNN-based detectors.
applications.quote: such as face detection [8] [5], pedestrian detection [9] [4] and etc [2] [1] [10]

deploymentClaims: UnitBox runs at about 12 fps on VGA-size images, versus seconds per image for DenseBox.
UnitBox processes more than 10 images per second owing to its single extra convolutional layer.
Authors claim the efficiency advantage makes UnitBox suitable for real-time detection system deployment.

evidence.quote: The advantage in efficiency makes UnitBox potential to be deployed in real-time detection systems.
the UnitBox could process more than 10 images per second, while DenseBox needs several seconds to process one image
